Better to think of a molecule: neopentyl glycol (2,2-dimethyl-1,3-propanediol) has formula C5H12O2, not.

Our formula C6H14O3 suggests 6 carbons, 14 hydrogens, 3 oxygens. For saturated acyclic, hydrogen count = 2C + 2 - (X) where X = number of heteroatoms? Actually heteroatoms like O don't affect H count. So max H for C6 saturated = 2*6+2 =14. So C6H14O3 is fully saturated, no double bonds, no rings. So all O are attached as OH (or ether).
